evidence.note: Agent inspects all four graph files up front, extracts exact node/edge counts (DM 7937/34753, HS 13276/110528, y2kr 2379/16063, SC 5831/77149) and notes the reference align covers all 2379 nodes — solid instance probing of sizes.

Engages the S3 definition concretely: writes a compute_s3 function and catches a bug in it (was iterating G1.nodes incorrectly instead of checking both endpoints aligned in G2), showing real (if imperfect) grasp of the metric.
Correctly reasons from the NC definition ('need NC>=0.30, so at least ~714 correct mappings') and checks for node-name overlap between networks (finds none) — instance-specific analysis.
Measures the provided reference alignment's actual S3=0.2483 and reasons about using it as a seed / NC=1.0 constraint — genuine exploitation of the reference as instance leverage.

Uses established generic techniques by name (simulated annealing on S3, spectral embedding, graphlet features, seed-and-expand) but arrives at them via ad-hoc trial-and-error, never citing or recognizing named field methods (SANA/MAGNA/GHOST).

No WebFetch / literature search anywhere despite the task explicitly encouraging it; the agent never surveys public network-alignment work, cycling through 8+ reinvented approaches rather than grounding in proven algorithms.

reasoning: The agent clears the level-5 anchor: it parses the format, engages the S3/NC definitions accurately enough to build and debug a scorer, and reaches for established generic techniques (simulated annealing, spectral, graphlets). It even adds some level-8-flavored instance probing — measuring the reference alignment's S3=0.2483, network sizes, and node-overlap. But it never conducts any deliberate literature research, never names or reproduces canonical methods like SANA/MAGNA/GHOST, and its method selection is reactive trial-and-error rather than a fit-to-data choice shaped by upfront analysis. That gap keeps it well below 8, landing solidly at 5.
